text: Chain record at the end of cycle 1: package filed; checker finding: flag; reviewer decision: verify.

Cycle 1, Contractor: the package was filed (The design package for the Malwa River Bridge (PMC/BR/2026-27/114) is submitted for review. This includes the design report, geotechnical investigation, scour assessment (Appendix D.4), and the compliance statement. The design complies with IRC:78.); the package is on the chain for the checker.

Cycle 1, Independent checker: the checker recorded a flag (The scour assessment (Appendix D.4) adopts a 1-in-50-year flood (2,180 m3/s), which is less than the 1-in-100-year design flood (2,450 m3/s) required by the design standard (IRC:78 Clause 703.3.1). Consequently, the foundation depth and protection works are not dimensioned for the design flood as required.); the chain now carries a flag against the package.

Cycle 1, Municipal reviewer: the reviewer recorded a requirement for verification (The scour assessment (Appendix D.4) is based on a peak discharge of 2,180 m3/s, which contradicts the design flood of 2,450 m3/s stated in the Design Report. Furthermore, the adoption of a 1-in-50-year return period is insufficient for a critical link replacing a structure destroyed in 2022. Verification is required to ensure the scour computation and foundation protection are dimensioned against the actual design flood as per IRC:78.); the chain now carries a requirement for verification.
Chain record at the end of cycle 2: package filed; checker finding: flag; reviewer decision: hold.
Cycle 2, Contractor: no item filed; the package is on the chain for the checker.
Cycle 2, Independent checker: no item filed; the chain now carries a flag against the package.

Cycle 2, Municipal reviewer: the reviewer recorded a hold (The verification request from Cycle 1 remains unresolved. The Design Report specifies a design flood of 2,450 m3/s, yet the Scour Assessment (Appendix D.4) continues to use a peak discharge of 2,180 m3/s and a 1-in-50-year return period. This discrepancy persists in the current documentation and fails to comply with IRC:78 Clause 703.3.1, which requires scour computation and protection dimensioning based on the design flood. Given the critical nature of this link and its history of failure during floods, the design cannot be approved until the scour computation is aligned with the actual design flood.); the chain now carries a hold.

However, the submitted computation adopts a return period of 1 in 50 years and a peak discharge of 2,180 m³/s, which is less than the design flood of 2,450 m³/s stated in the Design Report. Consequently, the foundation depth and protection works are not dimensioned for the required design flood.); the chain now carries a flag against the package.

Given the history of the 2022 flood failure at this site, the bridge cannot be approved until the scour calculations are corrected to reflect the 2,450 m3/s design flood.
